node-1.label: Patient presented with shortness of breath for 2 days

node-2.label: Patient was in their 60s, had no known medical history, and was not vaccinated against COVID-19

node-3.label: Illness progressed to acute respiratory distress syndrome requiring intubation and proning

node-4.label: Course was complicated by acute kidney failure requiring hemodialysis

why.why: Positive SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR directly confirms COVID-19, and CTPA showing multifocal ground-glass opacities without pulmonary embolism is characteristic of severe viral pneumonia. Combined with unvaccinated older age, ARDS requiring proning, and acute kidney injury, the evidence strongly supports severe viral pneumonia; both Radiology and Laboratory analyses agree. Confidence raised from 0.78 to 0.92.

New evidence of positive SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR and CTPA showing viral-type multifocal opacities without embolism shifts the etiology away from bacterial sepsis. Expert analyses note no bacterial pathogen has been identified, and the ARDS and AKI are already well explained by severe COVID-19, so bacterial pneumonia with sepsis is much less likely. Confidence reduced from 0.14 to 0.05.

Positive SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR and a viral pneumonia pattern on CTPA, with no pulmonary embolism and no identifiable non-infectious cause, make non-infectious ARDS unlikely. Expert analyses attribute the ARDS and AKI to severe viral pneumonia, so this hypothesis remains a remote alternative. Confidence reduced from 0.08 to 0.03.
